newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Falklands foes vow cooperation on S.Atlantic fish.
newsitem.headline: Falklands foes vow cooperation on S.Atlantic fish.

text.p: Argentina and Britain agreed in fishing talks in Buenos Aires to continue joint investigations into protecting fish stocks in disputed South Atlantic waters, the Argentine government said Wednesday.
Fishing has been a major sticking point in otherwise fluid relations between the two former Falklands War enemies.

But after two days' talks of the bilateral South Atlantic Fishing Commission, they issued a joint statement stressing the "constructive spirit" of the talks and expressing shared concerns about stocks, especially of the ilex squid.

Britain and Argentina went over the Falkland Islands, which Argentina calls the Malvinas, in 1982. They have since restored diplomatic and trade links and reached agreement on oil exploration in the British-run islands, which Argentina still claims as its own despite losing the 10-week war.
But a long-term deal on protection of fish stocks has proved elusive and squid catches have been falling sharply in recent years.

An Argentine Foreign Ministry statement said the talks, which followed a meeting of a scientific sub-committee in the seaside resort of Mar del Plata, "agreed to recommend to their governments to continue cooperating to reach a higher degree of scientific knowledge of the most significant species."
They plan an investigative cruise in South Atlantic waters next year to check on stocks of the squid, which are a major income source for the Falkland islanders.
But the Argentines included a complaint about Britain's decision in 1990 to expand its fishing exclusion zone around the islands.
